verdict.label: separate
verdict.why: Both functions convert normalized screen coordinates into NDC and cast a three.js ray, but that overlap is only generic three.js boilerplate (`x * 2 - 1, 1 - y * 2`, `setFromCamera`, `updateMatrixWorld`). The domain logic differs. NEW (phone) intersects a single display mesh, or a fixed plane while captured. It then maps local coordinates to clamped u/v and applies a rotation-dependent remap. EXISTING (duo) hit-tests multiple meshes, derives UV from triangle barycentric interpolation, tracks capture state keyed to a display, and delegates to `duoRawPoint`. Their capture handling, coordinate derivation and outputs are not the same operation. No concrete shared helper beyond trivial NDC setup is established.

source_adjudication.contract: No common nontrivial projection contract established. Phone computes local rectangular plane position, clamps and rotates; Duo selects display meshes, computes/stores triangle UV capture and extends through barycentric interpolation.
source_adjudication.existing_shared_owner: createDisplayProjection already owns phone/model projection; Duo does not call it. Existing helper cannot absorb Duo unchanged. Captured plane semantics and UV policy differ.
source_adjudication.independent_frozen_source_conclusion: Borderline; do not accept broad projection equivalence. Phone clamps local rectangular coordinates and rotates output; Duo identifies active mesh/panel, retains a world triangle/UVs and extends via barycentric coordinates. Shared camera ray setup alone is likely framework shape. Need a useful narrow owner argument beyond Raycaster before acceptance.
legitimate_variations: Keep mesh/display identity, captured plane frame, UV interpolation, clamp and output rotation semantics independent.
